title: From Exponential to Gaussian Tails: Fractal Wavefront Scaling and the $κ$-Weibull Distribution at Phase Transitions
authors: O. V. Pavlovsky, M. Yu. Satleikin
abstract: The paper examines the features of critical evolution in an active medium modeled by a cellular automaton. The system evolves according to stochastic rules, exhibiting two qualitatively distinct dynamical regimes: one of fading activity and another of all-filling activity waves. Each regime is characterized by its own fractal dimension and fluctuation statistics, both of which are analyzed in detail. Within the critical interval, the system displays a nontrivial fractal dimension and a fluctuation distribution that bridges the two regimes. This bridging behavior arises because, in the critical interval, the dynamics are governed by avalanches.
summary: This work analyzes a stochastic cellular automaton modeling an active medium undergoing phase transitions. It demonstrates that the system's fluctuation statistics transition from exponential decay (fading activity) to Gaussian behavior (wave filling), passing through a critical regime described by the $\kappa$-Weibull distribution. This connects macroscopic geometric properties, like wavefront fractal dimension, directly to microscopic statistical fluctuations.
main_problem: The paper investigates critical evolution, fractal scaling of wavefronts, and fluctuation statistics across phase transitions in an active medium.
main_result: The system exhibits a transition where the fluctuation distribution bridges exponential (fading) and Gaussian (wave) regimes, characterized by a $\kappa$-Weibull distribution at criticality.
method: Analysis involves studying fractal dimensions via scaling limits and fitting fluctuation probability density functions to identify underlying statistical laws.
model_or_system: The model is an active medium simulated using a stochastic cellular automaton on a planar square lattice, whose evolution depends on activation probability (G) and immune decay time (M).
key_observables: Fractal dimension ($D$) of the wavefront, fluctuation distribution $	ext{p}(\delta S)$ for sensitive cell concentration ($\delta S$), and system temperature ($T$).
important_parameters: Activation probability ($G$), Immune tail length ($M$), Critical point ($G_{cr}$), and lattice size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximating the PDF with specific functional forms (e.g., Weibull or stretched-exponential) to characterize the transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate dynamic equilibrium states, the sharp transition of fractal dimension near $G_{cr}$, and comparisons between Gaussian, Weibull, and general fluctuation distributions across different regimes.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes three distinct dynamical regimes (fading, critical, wave) by examining how the system's fractal dimension and fluctuation statistics change as a function of the control parameter G relative to $G_{cr}$.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the concept of phase transitions governing complex pattern formation and scaling laws is highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum many-body systems.
